The paper introduces a new strategy for simultaneous acoustic and electromagnetic invisibility using a combination of four conventional cloaking methods.
Two modes of cloaking are proposed: blind mode and deaf mode.
In blind mode, the object is electromagnetically invisible but acoustically detectable.
In deaf mode, the object is acoustically invisible but electromagnetically detectable.
The blind mode combines Acoustic Out of Shell Cloak (AOSC) and Electromagnetic Perfect Cloak (EMPC).
The deaf mode combines Perfect Acoustic Cloak (PAC) and Electromagnetic Out of Shell Cloak (EMOSC).
Transformation optics and transformation acoustics theories are used to design the cloaking structures.
Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) simulations were used to model electromagnetic wave scattering.
Acoustic wave scattering was simulated by mapping acoustic equations to Maxwell’s equations.
The blind mode AOSC core radius is 0.5 cm, complementary inner radius 1 cm, and complementary outer radius 1.6 cm.
The blind mode EMPC inner radius is 1.8 cm and outer radius is 2 cm.
The deaf mode EMOSC core radius is 0.5 cm, complementary inner radius 1 cm, and complementary outer radius 1.6 cm.
The deaf mode PAC inner radius is 1.8 cm and outer radius is 2 cm.
Metamaterials are necessary to achieve the required anisotropic and inhomogeneous properties for cloaking.
Perfect invisibility is theoretically impossible, but multi-cloaking reduces detectability by multiple detection methods.
The proposed method does not generalize to all pairs of physical phenomena, e.g., electrical-mechanical or thermal-mechanical combinations.
Out of shell cloaking allows cloaking of objects located outside the cloaking shell without interfering with the cloak.
In blind mode, electromagnetic waves do not penetrate the EMPC shell, preserving waveform and phase.
In deaf mode, acoustic waves are blocked by the PAC layer, preventing acoustic interaction with the object.
The method can potentially be extended to other dual cloaking applications such as electromagnetic-elastic cloaking.
